subject: Computer Networking
title: CSS — Styling the Web
description: A fast breakdown of CSS — Styling the Web for builders.

hook.text: HTML builds the skeleton. CSS paints it. Every color, font, and layout on the web comes from CSS.

buildup.text: Selectors target HTML elements. Properties set values: color, margin, font-size, display, and hundreds more.

discovery.text: The cascade resolves conflicts: inline beats internal, internal beats external. Specificity is the tiebreaker.

twist.text: Responsive design uses media queries. One stylesheet adapts the layout to phones, tablets, and desktops.

climax.text: Flexbox and Grid transformed layout. Before them, developers hacked layouts with floats and tables.

punchline.text: CSS makes the web beautiful. Separation of structure and style.

quiz.question: What CSS feature enables layouts that adapt to different screen sizes?

details.summary: CSS controls the visual presentation of HTML content, defining colors, fonts, layouts, spacing, and responsive behavior through selectors and declarations. The cascade mechanism resolves conflicts when multiple rules target the same element, using specificity, source order, and importance.
details.whyItMatters: CSS separates design from content, enabling consistent visual styling across entire websites. Modern CSS layouts with Flexbox and Grid replaced fragile float-based techniques with powerful, intuitive systems.
takeaways: CSS selectors target HTML elements for styling declarations
Flexbox and Grid provide powerful two-dimensional layout systems
Media queries enable responsive designs that adapt to screen size

faq.question: What is the CSS cascade?
faq.answer: When multiple CSS rules target the same element, the cascade determines which wins. It considers source order, specificity of selectors, and the !important flag. Inline styles beat stylesheets. ID selectors beat class selectors. Later rules beat earlier ones at equal specificity.

faq.question: How does responsive design work?
faq.answer: Media queries apply different CSS rules at different screen widths. Mobile-first design starts with styles for small screens and adds complexity for larger ones. Flexible units like percentages, viewport units, and CSS clamp adapt elements fluidly.
